## Summary

I built **Elder Realms**, a complete 3D open-world RPG in a single self-contained `index.html` (no install required — it loads Three.js from a CDN and runs entirely in the browser).

### Content
- **All 15 classes**: Warrior, Barbarian, Mage, Sorcerer, Warlock, Rogue, Ranger, Druid, Paladin, Cleric, Necromancer, Healer, Tank, Bard, Monk — each with unique base stats, HP/MP, and 3 class abilities (e.g. Power Attack/Rage/Fireball/Backstab/Heal/Taunt/Inspire).
- **All 11 races**: Elves, Humans, Dragonborn, Goblins, Halflings, Dwarves, Tieflings, Minotaurs, Angels, Fallen Angels, Demons — each with racial stat bonuses.
- Character creation with name, race/class selection, live stat preview, and starter gear.

### Gameplay
- **3D world** (Three.js): 42×42 tile world with biomes (grassland, forest, hills, mountains, water, swamp, village, dungeon, desert), procedural village, dungeon entrance, trees, and a moving camera that follows you.
- **Movement** (WASD/arrows), random encounters by terrain, turn-based combat with basic attack, class abilities, items, defend, and flee.
- **Systems**: XP/leveling, HP/MP regeneration in safe zones, inventory (20 slots) + equipment (weapon/armor/accessory), consumable potions, shop, NPC dialogue, quests (accept/complete with rewards), kill credit tracking.
- **UI**: HUD (HP/MP/XP/gold/zone), character panel, inventory, skills, quests, world map, save/load to localStorage, respawn at village.

### Verification
Launched the dev server and drove it with a real browser (Chromium headless via Xvfb). Confirmed:
- Page loads with HTTP 200
- Three.js initializes and the 3D scene renders (118KB screenshot, 1050×793 viewport)
- Zero JS errors (ReferenceError/SyntaxError/TypeError all resolved); only harmless Three.js deprecation and WebGL perf warnings remain

- Single-file HTML/JS build (no build step) since the environment serves static `index.html`.
- Three.js loaded from CDN (`unpkg.com`) — network is available at runtime.
- Save/load persists via `localStorage`.
- Combat is turn-based (real-time movement, turn-based fights) to keep it playable and complete in one file.
